LHX.sentence: L3Harris has fallen about 32% from its high, which is unusually steep for a defense company — but military spending keeps rising steadily, so nothing has really changed about the business underneath.

ASML.sentence: ASML drifted down a few percent this week, but they're still the only company on earth that makes the machines needed to print the most advanced chips, so the long-term demand story is intact.

LIN.sentence: Linde is essentially flat — when markets get nervous, investors tend to favor steady, dependable businesses like this one, and selling oxygen and nitrogen under long-term contracts is about as steady as it gets.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is quiet and holding up better than most tech names in a jittery market — the cloud-and-AI story keeps grinding along without any drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher has nearly recovered to its high, so the cheap buying window has closed, but the business of selling lab equipment and supplies to researchers keeps chugging along fine.

CVX.sentence: Chevron edged up, and its profits look big mainly because fighting involving Iran has pushed oil prices well above normal — that's the oil price doing the work, not the company itself, so it's priced about fairly rather than being a bargain.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow has been cut nearly in half from its high, which is rare for a company still growing fast — either a remarkable buying chance or the market sniffing out a problem, but companies keep signing up for its workflow and AI tools on long-term contracts.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore jumped about 4% and is holding up better than copper prices alone would suggest, because its trading arm keeps making money even when metal prices are washed out, all while paying a hefty dividend.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta is steady, and the number that actually matters — the price they get per ton of crushed stone — is still climbing nicely, even though a shift in their sales mix makes the headline price look like it fell.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA is fine operationally, but a weakening Mexican peso eats into its earnings once they're converted back to dollars, which is the main thing weighing on it.

UBER.sentence: Uber held steady and people keep booking more and more rides and food orders, with no sign yet that self-driving cars are pulling business away — the next real read comes with its early-November report.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the Danish container-shipping giant, is trading below what its fleet of ships would cost to replace, meaning you're essentially getting its logistics business thrown in for free.

MA.sentence: Mastercard climbed nearly 2% and people keep tapping their cards more than ever — it's trading unusually close to Visa, having lost the small premium it normally carries over its twin.

ISRG.sentence: The surgical-robot company jumped over 4% and sits well below its high, which looks fearful given that hospitals keep doing more operations with its machines and every surgery sells more supplies.

NVDA.sentence: Nvidia dropped almost 6% after two of its biggest customers, Google's parent and Amazon, revealed they're now spending more on computing gear than their businesses bring in and borrowing the rest — nothing changed at Nvidia itself, but whether those customers can keep paying is the entire question.
